mission: Timaeus uses singular learning theory (a mathematical theory of how neural networks learn) to understand how training data shapes AI behaviour, and how capabilities and values emerge during training. The aim is tools to steer training so models end up aligned. As Resolution it is scaling this with a large, automation-heavy alignment programme.

key_work.title: Loss Landscape Degeneracy and Stagewise Development in Transformers
key_work.plain_summary: Shows transformers learn in distinct stages that can be detected with singular learning theory, the start of 'developmental interpretability'.

key_work.title: SLT for AI Safety (research agenda)
key_work.plain_summary: Explains why the mathematics of how networks learn could give alignment a firmer scientific footing.

key_work.title: Spectroscopy at Scale: Finding Interpretable Structure in Pythia-1.4B
key_work.plain_summary: Scales Timaeus's 'susceptibility' tools to a real 1.4B-parameter language model and finds interpretable structure.

key_work.title: Patterning the Toy Model of Superposition
key_work.plain_summary: Demonstrates 'patterning': using interpretability to deliberately shape what a model learns during training.

key_work.title: Resolution: Scale and Automation for Higher Confidence in Alignment
key_work.plain_summary: Launch of the merged organisation, aiming at 40–80 staff within two years and much higher confidence in alignment before superintelligence is trained.

key_work.title: devinterp library
key_work.plain_summary: Open-source code for local learning coefficients, susceptibilities and related training-dynamics tools.

status_note: in June 2026 Timaeus joined researchers from the UK AISI Alignment Team to form a new organisation, briefly called Sequent and then Resolution; the legal entity Timaeus Research, Inc. became Resolution Alignment, Inc.

warnings.text: Artificial superintelligence may be developed in the next few years, and it is unclear whether alignment will be ready in time.
The empirical programmes at AI labs are unlikely to give confidence before training ASI that things will go well.

recommendations.text: Pursue higher-confidence alignment through a mix of theory and experiments.
Invest heavily in automating alignment research to speed it up.
Understand and control how training data shapes model values, rather than only testing finished models.
